status: captured, judged by 5 AI jurors from evidence packs and the owner (2026-11-01)

measured_cost.note: [seconds, subagent tokens]. Batch-002: about 20 min and about 720k tokens for 3 sites.

business.what: US direct-to-consumer breastfeeding kits and accessories (Latch Kit $99.99, Cloud 9 $65, Nips Duo $22) for pregnant and new parents, plus free education (video school, talk circles) and a newsletter.
business.action_that_pays: SHOP KITS; every featured kit was SOLD OUT at capture (2026-10-31)

claims.evidence: Simple in use: flat colour blocks, one ink colour (#8b2a00), 0 gradients, 0 shadows. Not few colours: 6 chromatic backgrounds, each section its own colour (works as chapter markers). The yellow H1 on the tan hero fails contrast (2.0-2.1:1).

claims.claim: Very balanced play of text sizes
claims.evidence: What works is contrast, not balance: a decisive jump from display (94-100px desktop, 58px mobile, Caslon Rounded) to 16px body (Roobert). 9 sizes on desktop, down to 10px.

claims.verdict: confirmed with correction (after a disagreement, settled by a measurement)
claims.evidence: No scroll library and only CSS transitions, which led three jurors to contest it. The motion juror saw a sticky 'curtain' reveal; a follow-up measurement found 4 full-screen sticky panels (bottom:0, stacked by z-index): each section uncovers the next. The technique is common CSS; what makes it Swehl's is the arch shape and colour per section.

claims.claim: CTA early, fixed at the bottom, with a circular radius
claims.verdict: partly right; two different elements merged
claims.evidence: The early CTAs (SHOP KITS, GET EDUCATED) are pill buttons (radius 9999px) in the middle of the hero, not fixed. The arched element fixed at the bottom is a newsletter pop-up (bottom sheet with an arched top) asking for email + due date about 1 s after load; it covers the H1 and the shop button. It is lead capture, not the action that pays.
claims.owner_clarified: The owner meant the arched-top pop-up: what they like is the shape (an arched bottom sheet). Library candidate: arched bottom sheet for lead capture, shown after scroll depth or exit intent, never over the hero in the first seconds.

library_candidates: Colour-coded chapters: one flat background per pillar, one ink colour for all text, no shadows or gradients
Arch shape framing curved display type over documentary photography ('LET'S TALK IT OUT')
CSS sticky curtain reveal between flat sections (no library, CLS 0, nothing hidden without JS)
Price inside the product title and the buy button
Optional due-date field on the lead form to time follow-ups (life-stage products)
Customer-voice copy: frank, warm titles ('Partners are People, Too.', 'Because Options.')
Marquee as table of contents right after the hero
Arched-top bottom sheet for lead capture (shape liked by the owner); trigger after scroll depth or exit intent, never over the hero
avoid: Pop-up over the hero and the paying CTA one second after load
Selling sold-out products with no restock date or waitlist
Proof that praises a different pillar than the one the hero sells

business.what: Personalised preventive-health / longevity programmes (diagnostics with 85+ biomarkers, doctors + AI, 100-day journeys) from Applied Healthspan Private Limited, India (inferred from +91 number and company suffix).
business.action_that_pays: Get Your Blueprint (sticky); no price on the page

entries.veto: Two vetoes. Accessibility: motion ignores prefers-reduced-motion (14 elements still move with the scroll, 4 on their own), 4 endless text animations incl. blinking 'LIVE NOW' with no pause control (WCAG 2.2.2), content that stays hidden. Business: unsourced health outcomes ('Reduced Cardiovascular Risk', 'Eliminate inflammation'), '10,000+ Personalised Journeys' and a 'HIPPA NPP Compliant' badge (misspelt; HIPAA has no official certification) presented as fact. The layout patterns may enter the library; the claims and the motion-without-static-path may not.

claims.claim: Every section is packaged with good scrolling
claims.verdict: confirmed with correction for the first ~60%; contested on 'good'
claims.evidence: Real machinery: GSAP, ScrollTrigger, SplitText, Lenis, Lottie; up to 13 script-driven elements per scroll step; each upper section has its own scene (hero zoom, spiral text, 3D head, card arc). Against 'good': no reduced-motion path, CLS 1.73 on desktop, 1-11 texts never visible during a scroll, header dropping with a white strip in 3 of 5 frames, empty bands while reveals are pending. Blog, FAQ and footer are plain blocks.

It is one 13,022px page, so these are transitions between sections. No page-transition library; the header link 'Our Approach' is an in-page anchor (a fully white frame after the click in the live check); the paying CTA goes to another subdomain without a transition. Lenis smooth scrolling is the likely source of the 'smooth' feeling; frame smoothness itself cannot be measured from stills.

claims.claim: Every section has a unique design
claims.evidence: True for the first ~60% (photo hero, arrows statement, 3D head with chips, fanned cards, burgundy sticky steps, human/AI diagram). From testimonials down the sections are standard. Variety without one idea: stock hiker, iridescent 3D head, gradient blobs and glass are the category's default look (distinctiveness capped at 5).

library_candidates: Fanned, tilted programme cards with each name as a wordmark over its own photo
Two-pole human expert vs AI copilot diagram meeting at the outcome
Problem then reframe pair ('Tired of one-size-fits-all health hacks?' / 'Your health doesn't live in silos. Neither do we.')
CTA label that is also a named step of the process ('Get Your Blueprint' = step 2)
Three-step How it Works with an INCLUDES list per step
Named clinical team with specialty and photo before the closing ask
Hero scroll-in that zooms the photo into the next section's background (only with a static path)
avoid: Scroll choreography without a reduced-motion path
Endless or blinking text with no pause control
Unsourced health outcomes and compliance badges
A promo bar for another product that outranks the main action
Coined jargon carrying the explanation (Centaur Team, Human 360 Body Data Stack)

owner_taste_signal: Third batch in a row where the owner's motion claims need correction (Maxima 'modern scrolling', Future 'animation in every section', Resolute 'page transitions'): the owner judges motion by feel, which the jury cannot measure from stills; the jury in turn missed a CSS scroll device until a measurement settled it. Both sides need a measurement of smoothness. Owner scores 2026-11-01: 9.5 visual and 9.5 ship for both sites, so the two-score format did not yet separate taste from client-readiness; across 11 references the owner has scored only 8-9.5.

owner_answers.swehl_cta: meant the arched-top newsletter pop-up (bottom sheet)
